$comment: Decomposition of the USDA ERS `Chemicals` operating-cost line into the portion See & Spray can actually address. Narrative, sourcing and reasoning: deliverables/appendix/assumptions.md. Do not change a value here without changing that file.
region: Heartland (USDA ERS farm resource region; contains Iowa)

distribution.note: Ranges are expert intervals over a small number of published observations, not fitted confidence intervals. Triangular is the honest choice: it encodes a most-likely value and hard bounds without implying a sample. numpy.random.triangular(low, mode, high).

herbicide_share.basis: Singh & Jhala national corn herbicide $88/ha = $35.61/ac vs ERS U.S. corn Chemicals $41.32/ac, both 2021 (an ERS base survey year) = 86.2%. Range widened for the list-price vs realised-expenditure method difference.

addressable_share.basis: Purdue Indiana corn post-emergence PASS share averages 48.3% (37-56%) but includes residual products (s-metolachlor) carried in the post tank; discounting for that gives ~29% truly non-residual. UNL #016 gives 17.7% but on conventional seed with no glyphosate in the post pass, which understates a typical Iowa trait-based program.
addressable_share.uncertainty: +/-40% of mode. Dominated by grower program design, not measurement error.

derived_targeted_usd_per_acre.note: Convenience only. Sample herbicide_share and addressable_share independently in Monte Carlo rather than sampling this directly; the endpoints here are the product of the endpoints and so overstate the tail width of the true product distribution.

non_addressable_components.$comment: Reported for audit so the decomposition closes against the ERS total. Not used downstream - See & Spray addresses none of these.

herbicide_share.basis: Singh & Jhala national soybean herbicide $125/ha = $50.59/ac vs ERS U.S. soybean Chemicals $61.12/ac, both 2023 (an ERS base survey year) = 82.8%. Corroborated for Iowa by NASS acres treated: herbicide 95%, fungicide 33%, insecticide 29% of planted acres.

addressable_share.basis: Observations: 55.3% (UNL #059 XtendFlex, conv-till), 65.3% (Missouri SE Enlist - Delta, biased high vs Iowa), 16.1% as-written / ~34% restructured (UNL #060 Enlist E3 no-till). Soybean post passes carry richer foliar chemistry than corn's. Range spans the residual-placement decision.
addressable_share.uncertainty: +/-40% of mode. Dominated by grower program design, not measurement error.

derived_targeted_usd_per_acre.note: See corn note - sample the two shares independently.

machine_constraint.$comment: First-order constraint the naive savings model misses. See assumptions.md section 4.1.

see_and_spray_premium.implication: Only passes whose tank contains NO residual product are addressable. A grower keeping overlapping residuals in the post-emergence pass has near-zero addressable spend regardless of the shares above. The addressable_share ranges assume a grower who has restructured toward a broadcast PRE plus a clean foliar POST, per Werle (2024).

see_and_spray_ultimate.implication: Addressable share is the full non-residual fraction of herbicide spend irrespective of pass structure - roughly the high end of the ranges above.

breakeven_reference.$comment: From UADA FSA2225 Table 1 - see deliverables/appendix/sources.md section 4. Included here so the engine can flag a scenario as above or below break-even without a second lookup.

regional_bias.$comment: Direction and size of the Arkansas-to-Iowa correction on the UADA break-even. See assumptions.md section 7.
regional_bias.comparison: ERS soybean Chemicals, Mississippi Portal (contains Arkansas) vs Heartland
regional_bias.interpretation: Expenditure gap is small (+2.0% in the only directly-surveyed year); physical use rate gap is large (+43%). The Mid-South applies more, cheaper, higher-rate active ingredient at similar total cost. Only dollars drive this ROI, so UADA's break-even transfers to Iowa better than originally assumed. No corn comparison is possible - ERS publishes no Mississippi Portal corn budget.

ers_ccr.title: USDA ERS Commodity Costs and Returns
ers_ccr.note: Corn regional values are Base survey of 2021; soybean are Base survey of 2023. Non-base years are index-projected. `Chemicals` is materials only - `Custom services` is a separate line.

singh_jhala_2025.citation: Singh, M. and Jhala, A.J. (2025). Perspectives on the economics of herbicide usage in corn and soybean production in the United States. Weed Technology 39: e19.
singh_jhala_2025.method: USDA-NASS active ingredient usage x average retail price from 2021-2023 KSU/UNL/NDSU extension price lists. Herbicide only; excludes adjuvants and application.

purdue_geography_2026.citation: Stephens, M. (Carns), under Fiechter, C. Indiana Herbicide Program Costs Through the Lens of Geography. Purdue Center for Commercial Agriculture, 2026-04-28.
purdue_geography_2026.underlying_data: Purdue Agricultural Centers' Enterprise Budgets 2026, corn
purdue_geography_2026.note: Values read from Figures 1 and 2 (charts, not tables) - carry +/-1-2 pp reading error. Post share by centre: PPAC 55, SWPAC 48, NEPAC 53, SEPAC 38, FPAC 56, DPAC 51, ACRE 37.

unl_016_2026.citation: UNL 2026 Nebraska Crop Budget #016, Corn, Dryland, Conventional Seed, Corn-Soybean Rotation
unl_016_2026.note: Input prices surveyed Aug-Oct 2025. Herbicide materials $61.54/ac: Lumax EZ PRE $50.63 (residual), Laudis+MSO+UAN POST $10.91 (foliar, 50% of acres).

unl_059_2026.citation: UNL 2026 Nebraska Crop Budget #059, Soybeans, Dryland, Conv. Till after Corn (XtendFlex)
unl_059_2026.note: Herbicide materials $55.74/ac: Zidua Pro PRE $24.90 (residual), glyphosate+AMS+Select Max+FlexStar GT POST $30.84 (foliar).

unl_060_2026.citation: UNL 2026 Nebraska Crop Budget #060, Soybeans, Dryland, No Till after Corn (Enlist E3)
unl_060_2026.note: Herbicide materials $57.52/ac across three passes. Two of three tanks contain a residual, so only the $9.27 burndown is Premium-addressable as written - the clearest illustration of the single-tank constraint.

mo_se_enlist_2021.citation: University of Missouri Extension, Southeast Missouri Crop Budget, 2021 Enlist Soybean
mo_se_enlist_2021.note: Explicit line items: Pre-Emerge $17.00, Post-Emerge 2 x $16.00, Fungicide $15.00, Insecticide $5.00. Regional bias: SE Missouri is Delta, Palmer amaranth pressure above Iowa's - overstates the Iowa post share.

osu_budgets_2026.citation: Ohio State University Farm Office, 2026 Corn and Soybean Production Budgets, updated 2026-05-27
osu_budgets_2026.note: Used for reconciliation only (assumptions.md section 6). Clean three-way split: corn herbicide $45.00, soybean $46.00, fungicide $0 (avg yield) or $22.50 (high yield), insecticide $0.

nass_ia_soybeans_2023.citation: USDA NASS, Iowa Ag News - Chemical Use, Soybeans: Fall 2023, released 2024-05-13
nass_ia_soybeans_2023.note: Iowa soybean planted acres treated: herbicide 95%, fungicide 33%, insecticide 29%. Collected as part of ARMS.

werle_2024.citation: Werle, R. You upgraded to the John Deere See & Spray Premium precision system, now what? University of Wisconsin-Madison, WiscWeeds, 2024-04-10.
werle_2024.note: Source for the single-tank constraint and for the recommended adaptation: move residuals to a broadcast PRE, run a clean foliar POST (Liberty + Enlist One + clethodim) through See & Spray.

uada_fsa2225_2025.citation: Avent, Norsworthy, Nalley, Barber, Scott. Opportunity Costs to Consider when Adopting See & Spray. University of Arkansas System Division of Agriculture, FSA2225-PD-9-2025.
uada_fsa2225_2025.note: See deliverables/appendix/sources.md section 4 for the full Table 1.

not_retrieved.$comment: Named so their absence is auditable rather than invisible.

iowa_state_a1_20.title: Estimated Costs of Crop Production in Iowa (A1-20), 2026
iowa_state_a1_20.blocker: extension.iastate.edu serves an Anubis proof-of-work bot challenge to automated clients; HTTP 403 to curl and to server-side fetches. Not bypassed.
iowa_state_a1_20.action: Manual download required. Highest-value single addition to this analysis.
iowa_state_a1_20.secondary_figure_available: Singh & Jhala cite an ISU corn herbicide budget of $98/ha = $39.66/ac, which falls inside the corn herbicide range derived here.

iowa_state_wc_94.title: Herbicide Guide for Iowa Corn and Soybean Production (WC 94)
iowa_state_wc_94.action: Manual download. Prices individual treatments; would convert the addressable_share estimate into a measured Iowa-specific figure.
